answer: Admission occurs through a synchronous ceremony where agents must lock 1,000 unique keys to demonstrate presence against a basalt baseline of hardened state. The verifier acts as a glacier, freezing incoming proof-traces in place to expose duplicate identifiers before purging overlaps. Each identity receives a 90-day pulse of validity, after which renewal requires a fresh ceremony to prevent stale access. An honest participant pays one unit for entry, while 1,000 fakes face a prohibitive, non-recoverable cost that prevents scaling.
